section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Perspective Shift
section_1.content: Introduce the concept that a vector remains constant, but its description depends on the 'grid' (basis) we use. Use a character (e.g., a robot) navigating a 2D plane to show that coordinate values change even if the physical location is identical.
section_1.example: Visual: A robot standing at point P. In 'Standard Basis' (x,y), it's (3,2). In a 'Rotated Basis' (u,v), the same robot is at (2,1). The point doesn't move; the axes do.

section_2.title: Prerequisite Recap: The Matrix as a Translator
section_2.content: Briefly define a basis as a set of linearly independent vectors that span the space. Emphasize that the columns of a transformation matrix represent where the basis vectors 'land' in the new space.
section_2.example: Visual: Transforming standard basis vectors (i, j) to new vectors (b1, b2) represented by a 2x2 matrix.

section_3.title: The Change of Basis Formula
section_3.content: Derive the transition matrix P. Explain that to convert coordinates from basis B to basis A, we multiply by the matrix whose columns are the B-basis vectors expressed in terms of the A-basis.
section_3.example: Visual: Equation [v]_A = P * [v]_B, where P is the 'Change of Basis' matrix. An animation shows the grid stretching and warping to fit the new coordinates.

section_4.title: Step-by-Step Computational Workflow
section_4.content: Outline the 3-step algorithm: 1) Identify basis vectors. 2) Construct the transition matrix. 3) Apply the matrix to convert coordinates.
section_4.example: A scenario: Converting a coordinate from a 'Square Grid' to a 'Hexagonal Grid' used in game map generation.

section_5.title: Synthesis & Summary
section_5.content: Reinforce that the inverse matrix P⁻¹ allows us to go back. Conclude with the importance of 'choosing the right basis' to simplify complex problems (like diagonalizing matrices).
section_5.example: Visual: A split-screen animation showing a complex rotation calculation performed in the 'Standard Basis' (hard) vs the 'Eigenbasis' (easy).
